but most people get the same mid result: centered text, gradient background, everything fading in. That's Opus's default look when it has nothing to copy.

here's the pipeline that makes it look like an agency did it:

1. Build the brand brain first
→ logo, colors, fonts, screenshots of your real product, your best ad copy
→ have Opus turn it into a DESIGN.md. The video and the site both follow it

2. Steal a reference, don't describe one
→ pick 1-2 launch videos with the pacing you want
→ "make it like this" beats "make it modern and punchy" every time

3. Give it a renderer
→ install HyperFrames or Remotion: every scene is code, rendered straight to mp4
→ a change = one line and a re-render, not starting over

4. Use real components
→ buttons, cards and UI from 21st_dev instead of empty placeholder boxes
→ fake-looking UI is the fastest way to look cheap

5. Storyboard before motion
→ 3 storyboard options, you pick one, then one still per scene
→ fixing a still takes seconds, fixing a render takes a re-render

6. Run it as a 4-person team + jev
→ breakdown: pull pacing, type and transitions from the reference
→ storyboard: the 3 options and the stills
→ build: every scene in code, music, draft render
→ review: watch it second by second, list the problems, touch nothing
→ jev: scores every review note against DESIGN.md (fix now / later / skip) in milliseconds, so build only touches what matters

7. Cut the ads from the same project
→ same scenes, different hooks: pain first, result first, offer first
→ 9:16 for reels, 1:1 for feed, 16:9 for YouTube. No reshoots

8. Ship the landing page from the same DESIGN.md
→ the hero is a looping cut of the launch video
→ before launch: mobile, every button state, zero placeholder text

9. Give notes like a director
→ "slow this zoom by half", "hard cut here", "push in on the button"
→ "make it better" gets random changes

text:
opus 5.5 is f*cking insane at motion design

every frame is code with 0 external tools

im open sourcing the template for all these morph transitions

steal it ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word, it becomes a black wordmark with a period), the one job a user hands it before bed, the three results it reports by morning, two photos of the same place at night and by day (aligned, so a crossfade reads as a real sunrise), one sunny daytime photo for outside the logo, and a song with a big hit near its start. If I skip any, use the defaults: "nightshift", "book 10 sales calls this week", 200 leads found / 200 emails sent / 10 calls booked.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 24 second square product launch video, 1440x1440 at 60fps, 2D only, one continuous take that loops. The whole video happens inside the period of the wordmark. Outside it's daytime (the sunny photo behind a black wordmark). Inside it's the night photo under iOS-style glass panels (the blurred photo behind each panel, a tint, a rim light). Nothing cuts: every scene grows out of the last, shapes morph, dots fly, colours change under floods. Every morph glides 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1) and the camera zoom rides the same curve. Geist, the real macOS pointer, soft shadows that grow with each shape's height.
Banned: flat or gradient backgrounds made in code, camera zooms into tiny points, hard cuts, crossfades between scenes, bouncy springs, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, cropped type.
</direction>

<structure>
Beats are the song's. The song enters on its big hit as the first pill appears.
Open: the letters slide into the period and vanish into it while it glides to the middle. The period opens like an iris onto the night inside it, and "you log off at 6", then "[product] doesn't", roll through one mask line over the night photo.
Ask: a glass "Ask [product]" pill springs in. The cursor clicks it, it glides into an input and the job types out.
Find: send shrinks the input to a dot that ripples into a 23x15 grid. A scan line sweeps it, 200 dots light up and a counter counts them.
Write: the lit dots pour into a glass email composer. A second, purple cursor labelled "[product]" types a personal opener and presses Send, and the counter runs to 200/200.
Night: the composer becomes a glass orb with a progress ring. A clock chip swaps 11:42 PM, 3:17 AM, 5:02 AM, 6:59 AM while the sky relights from night to dawn and "while you sleep" rolls in.
Results (beat 20): the orb turns black and goo-splits into the three result pills. The checks pop green.
Morning: the pills merge into a Dynamic Island that grows into a phone lock screen: the day photo, the date, a big 7:00, the bezel growing out of the screen edge. Three glass notifications stack in, and the cursor taps the first, which opens like iOS.
Proof: a week calendar (10 meetings pop in, a hover shows one's time), then a pipeline chart ($48,200 counts up, the line draws, a hover follows it). A black flood from the line's end becomes "Start your night shift →" and the cursor clicks it.
Out: the button shrinks into a dot, the whole scene closes down into it like an iris, and the letters slide back out of the period. The tagline rises. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Everything is a pure function of time inside seek(t): no timers, no state between frames.
2. One element morphs through every state (size, radius, colour, material) from a table of beat times, so retiming is one edit.
3. Render the inside world into an offscreen canvas and reveal it through the period with a circular mask. Never zoom the camera into the dot.
4. Glass: a pre-blurred copy of the photo clipped to the shape, then a tint and a gradient rim.
5. Goo: blur + alpha threshold on an offscreen layer for the split and the merge.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event, each placed by its measured peak. The song enters on its hit. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 4 motion-blur subframes. Scan every frame for single-frame jumps and fix each one.
</build>

<gotchas>
A camera zoom into an off-centre dot swings sideways and spikes, so open the dot instead. Ease a closing iris by area, not radius, or its first frames jump. A helper that sets globalAlpha must restore the caller's, or fading cards pop. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's, or the digits smear.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, find, write, results, phone, out) before you render.
</start>

Claude Code tip: install huashu-art-motion and Opus 5.5 can draw animations in 𝟯𝟱 𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝘆𝗹𝗲𝘀 with code. Van Gogh's starry sky swirls. Dalí's clocks drip. And its delivery script rejects any film where almost nothing moves.

You can just ask for an animation in the style of Van Gogh, Monet or Bauhaus, an explainer animation to go with your voiceover, or a character walking through one famous painting after another. Hand it a reference animation and it first breaks down the cuts, the beat and what moves where in the frame, then recreates it in code.

𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻 𝟭𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝘂𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝘁, Opus 5.5 made this demo video from its 35 built-in styles. It runs from cave painting 40,000 years ago all the way to 2026. The room, the cat and the girl never change; only the style does.

17 that work for any subject: products, data, stories
→ Van Gogh, Matisse cut-outs, Seurat pointillism, Impressionism
→ Analytic Cubism, Lichtenstein pop art, Bauhaus, Russian Constructivism
→ Ghibli watercolor backgrounds, Makoto Shinkai light, Chinese ink wash
→ 8-bit pixel art, vaporwave neon, 2026 flat illustration
→ Pompeii mosaic, early ray-traced CGI, Rembrandt chiaroscuro

18 for time travel, tributes and art-history speedruns
→ Monet's water lilies, Klimt's golden period, Munch, Dalí
→ Hopper, Picasso's blue period, Mucha's Art Nouveau
→ Keith Haring, Kusama polka dots, Jack Kirby comics, 1930s rubber hose cartoons
→ Cave painting, Egyptian tomb murals, Greek black-figure pottery, Dunhuang murals
→ Chinese shadow puppets, Gothic illuminated manuscripts, Renaissance sfumato

Each style spells out what moves in the picture. The eyes on Klimt's robe blink in turn, Hopper's hard-edged patch of sunlight slides slowly across a face, and the 8-bit question block pops out a coin.

9 explainer styles
→ For math and AI concepts, use 3Blue1Brown, where one shape morphs into the next
→ For data, use finance charts: axes first, then the data, and label only one thing
→ For UI steps in a software tutorial, use the keynote look: light-spot background, frosted-glass cards, big numbers
→ To draw relationships as you narrate, use the whiteboard, where the pen tip reveals the line art bit by bit
→ For a collage of graphics and info, use the Vox explainer look: clippings, red lines, highlighter
→ Kurzgesagt, flat with no outlines, moving between tiny and huge scales
→ Storytime, cutting to reaction close-ups and leaving a beat for the joke
→ Kinetic type, with the key word slamming into the frame
→ Presenter-led finance explainers, where you supply the character yourself

The music is synthesized in code too, note by note on a BPM grid. When a film is done, it runs its QA script, then sends an agent that took no part in making it to watch only the finished film and find problems. The delivery script also blocks two more things: 0.3+ seconds of blank frames mid-film, and a blue-purple background in over 30% of the film, a palette it counts as AI slop.

The skill has 𝗮 𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟱.𝟱 or stronger models, where it can combine the libraries itself and write its own renderers. All 35 styles are star-rated, and the 20 with three stars are recognizable at a glance and ready to use.

The skill's docs are in Chinese; the prompt below has it read them and talk to you in English.
Rendering video needs uv, ffmpeg and Playwright Chromium.
If you want people on screen, use your own character art or connect an image model to make the frames. Without either, it only draws hands and figures seen from behind.

npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion
https://t.co/tGUVjIj4FB

Once it's installed, send this to Opus 5.5 in Claude Code 👇

"Use huashu-art-motion to make me a 15-second animation. The skill's docs are in Chinese; read them and talk to me in English.
1. First check for uv, ffmpeg and Playwright Chromium, and tell me how to install anything that's missing.
2. Ask me what it's about, who it's for, and whether it's landscape or portrait. From the material layer in references/风格配方/INDEX.md, pick 3 styles that fit, three-star ones first. Redesign the composition for my subject in all three, each different from the others, and don't copy the room from the samples. Show me one still frame of each to choose from.
3. Once I pick, give each scene one main action plus two motif loops from that style's card. For Van Gogh, that's the starry sky curling into swirls and the lamp's halo spreading outward. If there's music, use the skill's BPM synthesis and put the motion on the beat.
4. If people need to appear, ask me first: my own character art, frames from an image model, or only hands and figures seen from behind.
5. After rendering, follow the skill's own QA steps: run its QA script first, then send a subagent that took no part in making it to watch only the finished film and find problems, have it write its findings into the 审片/ folder, and deliver with its delivery script. If anything comes up red, fix it and re-render before giving it to me."

7 video.
568.000+ görüntülenme.
5.120 abone.

Üstelik içeriklerin tamamı tarih üzerine hazırlanmış animasyon videolarından oluşuyor.

Kanalın adı: History in Minutes

Mantık oldukça basit.

Her videoda bir ülkenin bütün tarihini 15-20 dakikalık animasyonlarla anlatıyorlar.

→ The ENTIRE History of India
→ The ENTIRE History of Ukraine
→ The ENTIRE History of Russia
→ The ENTIRE History of Rome
→ The ENTIRE History of China

Başlık formatı aynı.

Thumbnail yapısı aynı.
Video konsepti aynı.
Sadece ülke ve anlatılan tarih değişiyor.

Bence burada asıl güzel olan şey tekrarlanabilir bir içerik formatı bulmuş olmaları.

Ve bugün Claude Opus 5.5 gibi modellerle bu tarz bir içerik üretim sistemini kurmak mümkün.

Mesela şöyle bir workflow oluşturabilirsiniz:

1. Topic Research

AI Agent, YouTube'daki benzer kanalları analiz eder.

Hangi ülkeler daha fazla izleniyor?

Hangi başlıklar çalışıyor?

Rakiplerin henüz işlemediği konular hangileri?

2. Script Generation

Opus 5.5 seçilen ülkenin tarihini araştırır.

Kaynakları karşılaştırır.

Kronolojik bir hikâye oluşturur.

15-20 dakikalık video senaryosunu hazırlar.

3. Scene Planning

Senaryo sahnelere ayrılır.

Her sahne için;

→ Görsel açıklaması
→ Karakterler
→ Mekân
→ Kamera hareketleri
→ Animasyon talimatları

oluşturulur.

4. Visual Generation

Hazırlanan sahneler görsel ve video üretim modellerine gönderilir.

Burada Opus 5.5'in görevi videoyu doğrudan render etmek değil.

Bütün üretim sürecini yöneten beyin olmak.

5. Voice + Editing

AI seslendirme oluşturulur.
Sahneler birleştirilir.

Altyazılar, müzikler ve geçişler eklenir.

6. Publishing + Analytics

Başlık ve thumbnail alternatifleri hazırlanır.

Video yayınlanır.

Sonrasında;

Average View Duration
Audience Retention
Subscriber Conversion

verileri analiz edilerek sonraki içerikler optimize edilir.

Yani sistem:

Research → Script → Storyboard → Generate → Edit → Publish → Analyze → Repeat

I don’t think editors are over at all. 

I run 7 YouTube channels and am a creative director. 

I work with editors every day and will continue doing so. 

Opus 5.5, Astra, etc are powerful tools. They absolutely lower the barrier to enter content & uplvl editing. 

But editing alone is not enough to make good videos. 

And people who use AI to edit are likely newer to video creation, which means they will use AI to copy techniques they like instead of making something new

This means they will be derivative instead of original = less likely to grow 

People who have been editing for yrs will be supercharged. This means editing teams actually have a massive W from these tools, not an L 

They can create faster, be more distinct, and get more clients

Creative people who have been doing this for a while will be more likely to edit independently 

However, if they are making good revenue from content, they will still outsource editing

This is because editing requires mental load to manage

And oncam talent needs to focus on performance on camera. 

So a couple segments will use AI editing: 

- new/small creators (who didn’t have $ to pay an editor anyways)
- existing creatives who are independent & dont want to hire (bad idea if making $) 
- existing creatives who want to learn editing 
- editors (ones who aren’t scared to upskill will win first)

Overall not expecting a massive change to editor revenue 

AI is giving specialists superpowers, not making them irrelevant

ROBLOX STUDIO + OPUS 5.5. A DICE-ROLL GAME WITH 170 BLADES, A DAILY SPIN AND A SUN-KING BOSS

OPUS 5.5 ROBLOX STUDIO IS INSANE PT.1 - the author's caption. The video is 4 minutes long, and it doesn't show one feature, it walks through a game that already has a collection, an economy and a boss

The author plays it live inside Studio and every screen is a different system

Collection: Backpack → 72/170 blades, and one of them is Clockwork Blade (Rare, Lv. 3): Damage 57, Attack Speed 0.78s, Range 13, Critical Chance 11%

Economy: $1.65M and 758 gems → ROLL, UPGRADES, AUTO and a 999x luck boost on the HUD

Daily Spin: a wheel with 6 prizes → 25 Coins 30%, 75 Coins 20%, 500 Cash 20%, 2 Gems 15%, 2500 Cash 10%, 10 Gems 5%

New weapon: Now wielding Nullrift! → a purple mythic blade, which then appears in a separate window as a 3D model made in the same session

Combat: Lv. 15 Gloam Magus 442/442 → then LEONIS, SUN-KING with a Lv. 63 Guardian Lion at 640/640

Here's the point

Look at the Daily Spin. The odds add up to exactly 100%, and the best prize has the smallest chance. That's not a visual, that's a designed drop table

The same goes for the blade card. Four stats, a rarity, a level, a collection counter. Every item is data the game can read, compare and upgrade

And the Nullrift blade isn't a pre-made asset. The chat on screen shows an edit to the 3D model, a re-export and a re-run of the setup file, with the session limit at 97%

People think AI in Roblox means one script and one model

This is a loop with a rarity system, a spin, a shop and a boss

Save this post

A game isn't built by one prompt, it's built by the systems that talk to each other

Love seeing all the feedback on @carlabotcoin’s debut music video. For those curious about what AI tools we used, here’s a breakdown below. But instead of just telling you, I can show you, so I had Claude make this video: "The Making of Carla Botcoin"

Here's the full stack:
TL;DR: Claude + Higgsfield + Suno + a manual final edit in Final Cut Pro by @CarlaBitcoin

• Claude Opus 5.5 (@claudeai): studied Carla’s real lyrics, wrote the song from my title “Fiat Is Fucked, Got Bitcoin?”, then ran the whole production. It also built us a library of custom skills and looks for Carla that mix film techniques, director styles and color schemes. The video uses a bright 1950s Luhrmann-style look built just for this song. 

Shoutout to @anabology for making his Slopcore / Claudia setup publicly available. We didn’t use it directly, but it was a helpful starting point, especially for measuring lip sync.

• @sunomusic: the music and Carla’s singing voice. Took a few of her songs as the reference before one clicked. Now it’s extremely true to her actual voice.

• @higgsfield: Claude’s Higgsfield connection is how we reached all the other AI tools: Seedance, Kling 3.0, Nano Banana Pro and more. Soul 2 + Carla’s Soul ID made every still and keyframe. I also had Claude build me a custom dashboard and rating system, completely separate from @higgsfield_ai, to dial in Carla’s likeness over many, many rounds of generations. My ratings feed back into how Claude builds her, so the more we generate and the more I rate, the better it gets at making Carla look like Carla, and at spotting when she doesn’t.

• Seedance 2.5: lip-synced singing. Great sync, but it redraws her face. The more she sang on screen, the less she looked like Carla.

• Take 2 and @Kling_ai lip sync: tried both, didn’t get the motion right.

• @Kling_ai 3.0: dance and movement shots. Held her face better than anything else. Surprisingly good.
• Nano Banana Pro: cleaning up stills, like stray lettering. Quick and reliable.

• ChatGPT (@OpenAI): first storyboard drafts. Useful to start, but we ended up scrapping all four boards.

• Demucs and Whisper: pulled Carla’s vocals out of the song and timed every word for the lip sync. Worked great.

• Final Cut Pro: Carla’s manual final edit.

Now, go give @carlabotcoin a follow 👇
